The record's +0x58,+0x60,+0x68,+0x70,+0x78,+0x80 come from six hash maps ([builder+0x30], keys = hash of the car name, mode 0/2/3/4/8/9 of 0x1405ed3a0) and are stored as 0 when the name is in no map. Ai_Job_UpdateCarsParallel passes them to Ai_LineCache_UpdateIfChanged (+0x58) and the table cursor updates (+0x60..+0x80) with no null check: ACCESS_VIOLATION reading 0x178 for a third car in My Team. Core's ai line set guard copies the pointer of the first record that has one into each null slot of the record just pushed. L1: needs the owner's L2 and an independent agree before it exports (the guard stays off until then).  | L2 ai-re 2026-11-03 own read: builder rbx = the 0x1a8 object from 0x1405ff947 (join code itself uses [rbx+8] at 0x1406004e4; regrow path stores [rbx+0xa8..0xb0] at 0x140602b00 then jmp). Both paths finish the whole record (+0x58..+0x80 at write time) before the end pointer moves, so last = [rbx+0xb0]-0x508 is the pushed record. Slots are map values (entry+8), consumers (Ai_LineCache_UpdateIfChanged, 14068ab50, 14068fb80, 1406925d0, 140697940, 140695330) only read the shared object and write the per-record cursor at record+0x88/0xf8/0x158/0x190/0x1c8/0x208; regrow memcpys records and frees only the buffer; same-name cars already share pointers. +0x78 is the only slot 14063e370 null-checks (0x14063ed4c), so the guard fills it only when +0x58 was empty
